title: Early Warning Signals Can Vanish or Amplify: Dimensionality in Complex Systems
summary: Early warning signals (EWS), such as increasing variance and autocorrelation, are widely used to anticipate critical transitions associated with saddle-node bifurcations. However, real-world systems are often high-dimensional and multiscale, potentially altering the classical behavior of EWS. Here, we investigate how dimensionality, inertia, and red noise influence the detectability of EWS prior to tipping points.
